title: Compose and publish a mushroom-jazz beat
description: Exercise the mushroom-jazz score-writing skill by composing, rendering, and listening to a new Apricity beat inspired structurally by the existing Salamander beat. Publish the approved .apr text as a new authenticated production Score record.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Studied the Salamander beat: one re-pitched one-shot clip per drum, assembled into a named kit, then played in a clear step pattern. The first mushroom-jazz sketch will keep that durable drum-kit structure but use a slower 92 BPM hip-hop pocket, a minor seventh progression, and sparse organic layers.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Built and auditioned a 16-bar 92 BPM mushroom-jazz sketch using the Salamander one-shot kit. The initial harmonic loop created broad chromatic clashes; a four-candidate swap audition selected a different loop that raised the checker objective from 79.8 to 94.1. The latest render has a clean compact drum pocket and a remaining mild +9-cent tuning guard, ready for listener feedback before production publication.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Listener rejected the first render as truly terrible, describing the dominant sound as a cash-register drawer or pinball machine. Diagnosis: the harmony layer was ccmixter/speck/household-hits_36991.mp3 loop-2, selected by the harmony checker despite being an obvious timbral mismatch. This confirms that the mushroom-jazz skill must treat source identity and ear-led auditioning as a hard gate; the next draft will not use household-hit material.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Rebuilt the sketch from scratch after the listener rejection. The household-hits loop, previous bass, and voice are gone. The new render uses the previously ear-approved ccmixter AlexBeroza Emerge loop as the sole musical scene, the Ave low held note for bass, and a deliberately quiet Salamander kick/rim/ghost/hat pocket. It compiles cleanly and has no checker guard violations; the next listening decision is whether the source and pocket now feel musically appropriate.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Rendered and measured three otherwise identical Amber Window versions. A (Ave bass) scored 89.3 with a 0.145 worst-span clash. B (same-source Emerge bass) scored 96.8 with a 0.062 worst-span clash and no guard violation. C (no bass) scored 98.0 but tripped the coverage guard because removing the bass artificially improves consonance while leaving Fmaj7 underrepresented. Measurement-led recommendation: B; listener will choose by ear.

comments.author: home
comments.text: The production app requires the score owner's Google/Cognito sign-in to create a Score. The production tab is open at the Google account prompt; publication is prepared but not submitted because no account credentials were provided.

comments.author: unknown
